profile: PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2 under the pinned native UPDATE profile.
scope: An ordinary single-target UPDATE can return named int4 fields of each updated row. The predicate and assignment reads see the old row. The output fields see the new row.
composition: Update owns an empty or ordered list of at most 1024 returned fields. The output fields reuse the checked single-target slot role and native rendering from DELETE RETURNING. Read, write and output slots all belong to the same resolved target. An output slot can read either a written or unchanged int4 field. Multiple new rows with equal projected values remain repeated.
observations: Compare physical rows in the target, inherited child and independent control relation, affected count, trigger events with old and new fields, and restored state.
Compare exact item order in the output layout, resolved labels including duplicates, native int4 types, values, row multiplicity, and NULLs. The output row bag has no guaranteed order.
The fixture distinguishes the old row, the simultaneous assignment results and the affected row projected by RETURNING. Zero affected rows still expose the output layout.
The engine retains its normal runtime trigger and privilege behavior. The tested fixture instruments the native row values through an AFTER UPDATE trigger.

finite.completeness: Recover each identity of the four-way Cartesian product exactly once from the checked structure, independently of request order.

exploration.structure: Generate one or two simultaneous assignments with distinct writable slots and NULL, literal or old-column reads. Generate up to five returned fields in both orders with distinct and repeated names and slots. Vary target occurrence, predicate and inheritance policy.

open: General returning expressions and column types beyond int4, UPDATE FROM, modification CTEs and later release OLD/NEW aliases.
trust: Native PDO positional metadata and physical state observer
Independent simultaneous assignment model and new-row projection
Exact PHP value and boundary checks

Mutation/Update.role: Execute a checked single-target write and optionally project the updated fields.
Mutation/Update.structure: One resolved TableSource, ordered assignments, predicate, release and an owned list of returned target positions.
Mutation/Update.conditions: The Update constructor checks every write, old-row read, predicate reference and returned slot in its single target scope.
Mutation/Update.meaning: Select old rows for which the predicate is true, apply all checked assignments from the old row, and read the specified fields from the updated row.
Mutation/Update.externalInterpretation: Execute against the same relation and descendant policy including the native trigger and privilege rules.
Mutation/Update.sql: Write one absolute target and its assignments and filter, followed by named RETURNING fields in their recorded order.
